sources.use: Failure-mode review: peer output exchange can hang when rank send/receive ordering is not explicit. mlx2 instead specifies ordered envelopes and treats transport ordering as an implementation obligation. No source copied.
Runtime capability basis for a future ring transport. No source copied and no interaction with the upstream repository.

modifications: Original route-independent cluster, request, admission, admitted-token bound, state-revision, cancellation, abort and two-rank agreement contracts with CPU fault tests, plus a bounded two-rank MLX ring diagnostic. Any identity, revision, ordering or phase fault now terminally poisons the transaction before raising, so a rejected stale cancel cannot be followed by publishable work.

limitations: No scheduler or HTTP route uses this contract yet.
The ring diagnostic used two ranks on one M3 host; no cross-host model-parity evidence exists.
The diagnostic used a fixed projection and fault exchange rather than sharded model layers.
The initial contract is deliberately fixed at two ranks.

validation.protocol_fault_regression: CPU tests prove stale cancellation and every rejected identity/revision/sequence fault leave the transaction terminal and refuse later STEP/COMMIT.
